metaDescription: Black Behi pechay is a pechay variety. 30 to 35 days to harvest. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others. Free guide.
excerpt: Black Behi is a registered pechay variety, also sold or known as Black Behi White Stem. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. B.M. Domingo bred it. It takes 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Black Behi White Stem, this is the same pechay. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Black Behi pechay takes 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more. Its seller gives 30 to 35 days in the Seed Board record, Ramgo gives 25 to 30 days after sowing and Allied 25 to 30 days after transplanting.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pechay fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** Ramgo states a potential of about 30 t/ha.
**Fruit:** Leaves: dark green blades on white, juicy stalks, Allied describes heavy, even plants with thick stalks rising from a broad, compact base.
**Season:** All year (Allied recommends it for the dry season).
**Where:** Lowland to midland, the Seed Board row also rates it for high elevation.
Ramgo claims good tolerance to diamondback moth, leafminer, damping off and soft rot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the only pechay on the old Philippine Seed Board list, first in the list of varieties in the IPB UPLB/PCARRD pechay guide reprinted by DA Caraga, and still carried by both Ramgo and Allied Botanical (as Black Behi White Stem). These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual pechay on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Black Behi pechay

Pechay is ready in about a month, so it fits small plots and quick cash. Pick a variety that bolts late in the heat and stands rain. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Black Behi White Stem the same as Black Behi?
items.a: Yes. Black Behi White Stem is another name for Black Behi. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Black Behi?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
